Both PyPI pages loaded without any challenge or gate, and both are now in `corpus/inbox/`. Only slabx is the SLAB dense-gas model; slabs is an unrelated networking tool.

ROW 1 | pypi-slabs | SAVED hb107_pypi-slabs.md 13393 | 1.0.3 | Apr 30, 2026 | MIT ("This project is licensed under the MIT License"; License expression: MIT) | https://gitlab.com/netodata/simple-labs | no — "Automated network lab provisioning on GCP with containerlab and netlab"
ROW 2 | pypi-slabx | SAVED hb107_pypi-slabx.md 8720 | 1.0.7 | Sep 12, 2026 | MIT ("MIT, for this implementation … The original SLAB source is not included and carries its own non-commercial terms"; License expression: MIT) | https://github.com/lyullee/slabx | yes — "A Python reimplementation of the SLAB dense-gas dispersion model, verified against the original and evaluated against field and wind-tunnel trials"

Things to know about the clippings:
- **Markdown added:** I added headings, code fences and list markers to match the page's layout. The page's own text was not changed.
- **slabs diagram:** in the slabs file, the ASCII diagram is copied as the browser extracted it, and its column spacing was already lost by then.
- **Extra link and timestamp:** I added two things from the page's own markup that are not in its visible text. One is the slabx concept DOI link, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22023625. The other is the exact slabs release time, 2026-04-30 14:15:24 +00:00.
- **slabx licence link:** the LICENSE link on the slabx page is relative (`LICENSE`), and it is kept that way in the file.

Only these two inbox files were written. I closed the browser tab when done.
